about.title: About
about.techFooter: Bachelor Thesis · Bern University of Applied Sciences · 2026
about.s1Body: This comparison portal was developed as part of a Bachelor Thesis at the Bern University of Applied Sciences (BFH). The aim is to support parents and students in finding the right Gymnasium preparation course in the Canton of Zurich.
about.s2Body: The portal uses a weighted utility analysis (Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis). Users can define which criteria are particularly important to them — for example price, quality, flexibility or location. Based on these weightings, the providers are evaluated and ranked by total score.
about.s3Body: Course data is automatically collected via web scraping from the providers' websites and regularly updated. An AI-based self-healing mechanism detects structural changes on provider websites and automatically adjusts the scrapers. All prices serve as orientation — the current information on the respective provider websites is always authoritative.
about.s4Body: This work was created in the Business Informatics programme at the Bern University of Applied Sciences (BFH), Department of Business.

header.kicker: Bachelor's Thesis · Comparison Portal for Grammar School Preparation Courses (Zurich)
header.title: Comparison of Scraping Methods
header.intro: This analysis compares three scraping methods used in my bachelor's thesis to build a comparison portal for grammar school preparation courses: Puppeteer (browser automation), Bright Data (cloud service), and ScrapeGraphAI (LLM-based). The evaluation follows six criteria:
header.statusLine: As of: {date} · Data basis: {courses} courses, {providers} providers, {runs} runs

section1.title: 1. Completeness
section1.subtitle: How many of the expected courses and fields are actually extracted?
section1.intro: The completeness analysis covers two providers for which all three methods were implemented: Gymivorbereitung Zürich (26 expected courses) and Avidii (14 expected courses). It shows both the number of courses found and the fill rate of critical fields.
section1.liveDataTitle: Live data: Courses per provider and method
section1.caption11: Table 1.1: Number of extracted courses per provider and method (live data from database).
section1.caption12: Table 1.2: Field coverage for Gymivorbereitung Zürich (manually determined from scraper outputs).
section1.caption13: Table 1.3: Field coverage for Avidii (manually determined from scraper outputs).
section1.fullCoverageNote: Full three-way coverage exists for {count} providers ({names}). Field coverage shows that Bright Data outperforms the Puppeteer scraper on date fields (Puppeteer: not implemented for GZ), while ScrapeGraphAI covers langgymi well but loses kurzgymi date information.

section2.title: 2. Accuracy
section2.subtitle: Are the extracted values correct? Are formats converted properly?
section2.intro: While completeness quantifies how many values are present, accuracy shows how correct those values are. The following overview compares the extraction strategies of the three methods for the key fields.
section2.caption: Table 2: Comparison of extraction accuracy per data field.
section2.outro: The analysis shows that all three methods are equivalent for simple values (prices). Differences emerge with more complex conversions (date format, availability status): here the manual implementation of the Puppeteer scripts pays off, while Bright Data offers a clean middle ground between effort and accuracy. ScrapeGraphAI is highly dependent on prompt quality and page structure.

section3.title: 3. Reliability
section3.subtitle: How consistent are the results? How many runs fail?
section3.intro: Reliability measures how often a scraper run completes successfully and how consistent the results are across multiple runs. The following live data comes from the scrape_runs table.
section3.successRateTitle: Live data: Success rate per method
section3.caption31: Figure 3.1: Successful vs. total runs per method (live from database).
section3.caption: Table 3: Qualitative risk analysis of the three methods.
section3.outro: In live operation, all three methods achieve a high success rate, but with different failure patterns: Puppeteer fails primarily on DOM structure changes, Bright Data on external timeouts, and ScrapeGraphAI on JSON parsing errors when the LLM returns invalid responses.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.body: The three scraping methods have different strengths: Puppeteer is the most reliable and most accurate, but requires the highest implementation and maintenance effort. Bright Data is the fastest and lowest-maintenance method, but it is paid and highly dependent on the external service. ScrapeGraphAI has the flattest learning curve and the lowest code overhead, but is slower and less consistent.
